    <!-- Brand fonts: Inter for chrome/text, JetBrains Mono for numbers + code.
         display=swap avoids FOIT; preconnect shaves the TLS handshake.
         referrerpolicy=no-referrer: these third-party font requests are
         discovered by the browser as it parses <head>, BEFORE the
         __skipAnalytics guard script below runs, so on a cold-load of
         /redeem/:code the stylesheet fetch would otherwise send the bearer
         voucher URL to fonts.googleapis.com as the Referer. Strip it — Google
         Fonts needs no referrer — closing the same leak the JS analytics guard
         closes for GTM/Meta/Crisp (codex round-21 P2). -->
    <link rel="preconnect" href="https://fonts.googleapis.com" referrerpolicy="no-referrer" />
    <link rel="preconnect" href="https://fonts.gstatic.com" crossorigin referrerpolicy="no-referrer" />
    <link
      rel="stylesheet"
      href="https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Inter:wght@400;500;600;700&family=JetBrains+Mono:wght@400;500;600&display=swap"
      referrerpolicy="no-referrer"
    />

    <!-- PWA install prompt: Chrome can fire `beforeinstallprompt` before the
         React app mounts, which would lose the event and prevent the custom
         "Add to Home Screen" banner from ever showing. Capture it early and
         stash it on window.__deferredInstallPrompt; AddToHomeScreen consumes
         it on mount. preventDefault() suppresses Chrome's default mini-infobar
         in favor of our banner. Gated to mobile viewports only — the banner is
         mobile-only, so on desktop we must NOT suppress the browser's native
         install UI (there is no replacement there). -->
    <script>
    window.addEventListener('beforeinstallprompt', function (e) {
      try {
        if (!window.matchMedia || !window.matchMedia('(max-width: 767px)').matches) {
          return;
        }
      } catch (_) {
        return;
      }
      e.preventDefault();
      window.__deferredInstallPrompt = e;
    });
    </script>

    <!-- Sensitive-path guard: runs BEFORE any analytics. /impersonate
         carries a single-use admin "View Account" bootstrap code in
         ?code=. We do NOT strip it here (the React route still needs to
         read it); instead we skip third-party analytics ENTIRELY on
         this path so GTM/Meta Pixel never capture the code via
         page_location/referrer. The /impersonate component scrubs the
         query from history right after reading it. Same treatment as
         /user/reset (reset token + email in URL) and /login/magic
         (passwordless sign-in token + email — MagicLinkConsume scrubs
         the query right after reading it). -->
    <script>
    (function () {
      var p = window.location.pathname || '';
      // Decode BEFORE every check below. Go decodes the request path, so
      // /%72edeem/SECRET routes to /redeem/SECRET and React Router mounts the
      // claim page — but window.location.pathname keeps the raw bytes, so a
      // trivially percent-encoded capability URL slipped every guard (codex
      // round 28). Decoding is safe in one direction only: it can introduce
      // path separators (%2F) and so only ever ADDS matches, never removes a
      // literal leading segment. A malformed escape fails CLOSED — we cannot
      // prove such a path is harmless, so suppress.
      var pDecodeFailed = false;
      try {
        p = decodeURIComponent(p);
      } catch (e) {
        pDecodeFailed = true;
      }
      // Collapse repeated separators, for the same reason and in the same
      // direction as the decode above (codex round 53). Every check below is
      // anchored with ^\/ and one separator per segment, so a hard load of
      // //compliance/share/TOKEN or //oauth/github?code=… — whose
      // location.pathname really does keep the doubled slash — matched none of
      // them, while the ingress (nginx merge_slashes, on by default) merged
      // them and served the real protected route. These tags run in <head> at
      // parse time, so nothing else can catch it first: round 52 normalized
      // helpers/pathGuard.js, but that is a MODULE and this guard runs long
      // before any module loads. Two parser-time copies exist for that reason
      // — this one and ssrBootGuardScript in controller/ad_tags.go — and they
      // are pinned against each other by TestSSRBootGuardMatchesShell.
      p = p.replace(/\/{2,}/g, '/');
      // Credential- or PII-bearing QUERY values, which no path check can see:
      // ?token= (any bearer), ?session_id= (the Stripe Checkout Session ID the
      // backend appends to the billing return, scrubbed only once React mounts
      // — the head tags run first), ?email=/?login_hint=/?focus_user_email=
      // (PKCEAuthorize copies login_hint into the login page's ?email=; admin
      // deep links carry a customer address), and ?redirect=/?redirect_uri=,
      // which can nest a token-bearing URL. Names are anchored on [?&] so an
      // ordinary ?promo_code= / ?aff_code= is unaffected. Bare ?code= is
      // deliberately NOT listed: /oauth/* is already path-guarded, and an
      // unqualified `code` elsewhere is far more likely an invite or affiliate
      // code — suppressing those would blind the very landings they measure.
      // Matched on DECODED KEY NAMES, not the raw query string. URLSearchParams
      // decodes keys, so the app consumes ?%73ession_id= as session_id while a
      // raw-byte regex sees nothing — the same raw-vs-decoded split as the path
      // above, and it survived the first fix (codex round 31). Split on the raw
      // & / = boundaries first (exactly where URLSearchParams splits), then
      // decode ONLY the key: decoding the whole string would let an encoded
      // VALUE containing %26/%3D forge parameter boundaries. A key we cannot
      // decode fails CLOSED.
      var SENSITIVE_PARAM_RE =
        /^(token|email|login_hint|focus|focus_[a-z0-9_]*|prompt|prompt_id|conversation_id|tool|tool_name|arg_paths|request_id|workspace_name|member_user_id|byok_key_id|client_app[a-z0-9_]*|run_id|guardrail_id|deployment_id|ws|skill_[a-z0-9_]*|redirect|redirect_uri)$/i;
      // session_id is sensitive ONLY on a checkout return. It is the Stripe
      // Checkout Session ID on /console/billing, but ActivityTab deliberately
      // uses ?session_id= as an ordinary firewall drill-in filter
      // (/console/firewall?tab=activity&session_id=…). Treating it as globally
      // sensitive meant an admin bookmarking or hard-loading that drill-in set
      // the DOCUMENT-STICKY __skipAnalytics, silently disabling tracking for
      // that page and every later SPA navigation in the same document — and
      // the real billing return strips its query without clearing the flag
      // either, so the suppression outlived its cause (codex round 48).
      //
      // Scoped by PATH PREFIX on the locale-stripped path, matched against the
      // decoded form for the same raw-vs-decoded reason as everything else
      // here. Narrowing rather than removing: on the billing return the ID is
      // still a live checkout reference and must not reach the tags.
      var CHECKOUT_RETURN_PATH_RE =
        /^(\/[A-Za-z]{2}(-[A-Za-z0-9]+)?)?\/(console\/billing|redeem)(\/|$)/i;
      var onCheckoutReturn = pDecodeFailed || CHECKOUT_RETURN_PATH_RE.test(p);
      /*
        THE ORCAPOOL INVITE CODE, on /models/<id>/pool?i=<code>.

        A permanent, reusable capability: whoever holds it can attribute a
        workspace to the referrer it names, and it neither expires nor
        rotates. A cold load of a shared invite link reaches these tags with
        the code in page_location before React mounts — GA/GTM/a pixel, a
        third party with its own retention and its own readers (Rule 14). The
        server-side redaction added for the access log and OTel does not reach
        this sink, and attribution.js's reserved-parameter list protects only
        our own beacon.

        SCOPED BY PATH, like session_id above and for the same reason. "i" is
        one letter: treating it as globally sensitive would suppress analytics
        on any page that ever uses a one-letter parameter, which is a silent,
        document-sticky measurement loss. The pool page itself still measures
        — it is a public, indexed marketing page — and only a visit CARRYING
        an invite goes dark.

        "[\s\S]+" RATHER THAN ".+", because this path is DECODED before it is
        matched: "%0A", "%0D", "%E2%80%A8" and "%E2%80%A9" in a slug become
        real line terminators, and JavaScript's "." does not match those. The
        server still serves the SPA shell for such a URL, so ".+" left exactly
        this page unrecognised and handed the code to the tags — the same
        raw-vs-decoded split this file records elsewhere, arriving through a
        regex instead of through a prefix compare.
      */
      var ORCAPOOL_PAGE_PATH_RE =
        /^(\/[A-Za-z]{2}(-[A-Za-z0-9]+)?)?\/models\/[\s\S]+\/pool\/?$/i;
      var onOrcaPoolPage = pDecodeFailed || ORCAPOOL_PAGE_PATH_RE.test(p);
      /*
        AND THE SPELLING THAT PUTS THE WHOLE THING IN THE PATH.

        "/models/<id>/pool%3Fi%3D<code>" reaches the browser with an EMPTY
        location.search: the "?" is a path byte, so decodeURIComponent above
        turns it into a literal "?" sitting inside "p", and the loop over
        location.search below has nothing to walk. ORCAPOOL_PAGE_PATH_RE is
        anchored at "$", so it does not recognise that path either — and the
        server serves the SPA shell for it all the same. Result: the code is in
        page_location, both halves of the guard say "nothing here", and GTM /
        the pixels / Crisp get it.

        This is the same encoded-tail shape isOrcaPoolPageFolded in
        middleware/logger.go already handles for the access log. The log half
        was fixed and this one was not, which is the recurring form of this
        defect rather than a new one.

        DERIVED FROM THE PATTERN ABOVE, not written out again: the tail case is
        that same pattern with its "$" replaced by a query DELIMITER — literal
        or percent-escaped to any depth, see the note below. A second literal
        is a second thing to drift, and this rule has already drifted between
        copies twice. The test asserts the derivation actually
        substituted something, so a pattern that stops ending in "$" reds here
        rather than silently matching nothing.

        ANY TAIL, NOT A TAIL NAMING "i". Same fail-closed reading the log
        redactor uses one layer down: a tail that got here cannot carry an
        invite the product will honour (the SPA reads an empty
        location.search), so its only demonstrated use is smuggling the code
        past a name match — and refusing to ask which key is in it removes the
        spelling question entirely (Rule 25: bind to the shape, not the name).
        The cost is that "/pool%3Ffoo%3Dbar" goes dark too; the one spelling
        that reaches this honestly is a model id which itself contains an
        encoded "?" ahead of a "/pool" segment, and the access-log redactor
        already treats that the same way.
      */
      /*
        AND ONE DECODE IS NOT A FIXED POINT. `/pool%253Fi%253D<code>` reaches
        the browser with that spelling intact in location.pathname, and the
        single decodeURIComponent above turns it into `/pool%3Fi%3D<code>` —
        still no `?` byte, so a pattern anchored on one matched nothing and the
        code went to page_location with the tags installed (codex round 39).
        Every deeper spelling repeats it one level out.

        So the delimiter is a SHAPE: `?`, or `%(25)*3F` case-insensitively,
        which is what each extra round of percent-encoding produces. Greedy is
        safe because `25` never begins with `3`. middleware/logger.go's
        orcaPoolDelimiterAt is the same grammar for the log and OTel sinks.
      */
      var ORCAPOOL_ENCODED_TAIL_RE = new RegExp(
        ORCAPOOL_PAGE_PATH_RE.source.replace(/\$$/, '(\\?|%(?:25)*3[Ff])'),
        'i',
      );
      var orcaPoolEncodedTail = ORCAPOOL_ENCODED_TAIL_RE.test(p);

      /*
        AND THE CREATOR INVITE PAIR, on /creators (main, codex r47 P2).

        A separate page with a separate pair of parameters, kept beside the
        pool guard rather than folded into it: they scope different keys to
        different paths, and one regex answering for both would have to
        widen one of the two. controller/ad_tags.go carries the same pair of
        guards, in the same order, for the server-injected copy.
      */
      var CREATOR_INVITE_PATH_RE =
        /^(\/[A-Za-z]{2}(-[A-Za-z0-9]+)?)?\/creators(\/|$)/i;
      var onCreatorInvite = pDecodeFailed || CREATOR_INVITE_PATH_RE.test(p);
      // THE PLAYGROUND'S ?key= (codex PR #1727). The product's own links put a
      // numeric token ROW ID there, never the secret; anything else in it is a
      // pasted credential, and these tags run before React can strip it.
      // Path-scoped like the pairs above ("key" is an ordinary word elsewhere
      // and the flag is document-sticky) and value-scoped so the row-id links
      // keep measuring. Mirrors carriesPlaygroundSecretKey in
      // helpers/queryGuard.js.
      var PLAYGROUND_PATH_RE =
        /^(\/[A-Za-z]{2}(-[A-Za-z0-9]+)?)?\/(console\/)?playground(\/|$)/i;
      var onPlayground = pDecodeFailed || PLAYGROUND_PATH_RE.test(p);
      // AND THE WHOLE QUERY SMUGGLED INTO THE PATH (codex PR #1727 round 8):
      // /playground%3Fkey%3D… arrives with an empty location.search, so the
      // loop below has nothing to walk. Derived from the pattern above with its
      // end replaced by a query DELIMITER shape (? or %(25)*3F), as the pool
      // guard's encoded tail is. Any tail goes dark, whatever it names.
      var PLAYGROUND_ENCODED_TAIL_RE = new RegExp(
        PLAYGROUND_PATH_RE.source.replace(
          /\(\\\/\|\$\)$/,
          // Any descendant first: /playground/battle%3Fkey%3D… is a tail too
          // (codex PR #1727 round 14).
          '(?:\\/[^?]*?)?(\\?|%(?:25)*3[Ff])',
        ),
        'i',
      );
      var sensitiveQuery = false;
      try {
        if (PLAYGROUND_ENCODED_TAIL_RE.test(p)) sensitiveQuery = true;
        var pairs = (window.location.search || '').replace(/^\?/, '').split('&');
        for (var qi = 0; qi < pairs.length; qi++) {
          var eq = pairs[qi].indexOf('=');
          var rawKey = eq < 0 ? pairs[qi] : pairs[qi].slice(0, eq);
          // A MATCHING KEY WITH NO VALUE IS NOT A BEARER (codex round 33, P2).
          // The verdict below is DOCUMENT-STICKY for the whole SPA session, so
          // treating "?i=" as a capability costs every later pageview's
          // campaign and experiment reporting plus the support widget, and
          // protects nothing — there is no code in an empty parameter. Tested
          // RAW and never decoded: non-empty is the whole question, and
          // decoding would let an encoded value forge a pair boundary.
          // Mirrors hasQueryKeyMatching in helpers/queryGuard.js, which makes
          // the same change for the live-document half (Rule 18 — the two
          // copies answer one question and must not drift).
          var rawValue = eq < 0 ? '' : pairs[qi].slice(eq + 1);
          // AN ENCODED DELIMITER in the name (?key%3Dsk-…): there is no literal
          // "=", so the value reads as empty and the skip below would pass it.
          // A name that decodes to contain "=" is never a real parameter name;
          // on the Playground it goes dark (codex PR #1727 round 12).
          //
          // Judged on the FULLY decoded name, not on the raw spelling of the
          // delimiter: %25%33%44 is a "=" too (codex PR #1727 round 13). A
          // name that still carries % or + after the loop, or will not decode
          // (throws into the catch below), fails closed.
          if (onPlayground) {
            var pgRawName = rawKey;
            for (
              var pn = 0;
              pn < 9 && /%[0-9A-Fa-f]{2}|\+/.test(pgRawName);
              pn++
            ) {
              pgRawName = decodeURIComponent(pgRawName.replace(/\+/g, ' '));
            }
            if (/[%+=]/.test(pgRawName)) {
              sensitiveQuery = true;
              break;
            }
          }
          if (!rawKey || !rawValue) continue;
          // '+' encodes a space in query strings; normalize before decoding.
          var decodedKey = decodeURIComponent(rawKey.replace(/\+/g, ' '));
          if (SENSITIVE_PARAM_RE.test(decodedKey)) {
            sensitiveQuery = true;
            break;
          }
          if (onCheckoutReturn && /^session_id$/i.test(decodedKey)) {
            sensitiveQuery = true;
            break;
          }
          // The creator invite pair, path-scoped for the same reason
          // session_id is: `h` and `r` are one-letter names certain to mean
          // something harmless elsewhere, and __skipAnalytics is
          // document-sticky, so a global rule would silence tags across the
          // product. On /creators they are a named person's public handle and
          // our own outreach-recipient id, sitting in the address bar of a
          // page whose GTM/GA/pixel tags are parse-time <head> scripts — they
          // run before any React code, and nothing ever strips the params, so
          // every pageview of the visit reports them to third parties.
          // (codex r47 P2)
          if (onOrcaPoolPage && /^i$/i.test(decodedKey)) {
            sensitiveQuery = true;
            break;
          }
          if (onCreatorInvite && /^(h|r)$/i.test(decodedKey)) {
            sensitiveQuery = true;
            break;
          }
          // Tested on the RAW value: our links emit exactly a positive
          // integer, and an encoded digit is not that shape, so it fails
          // closed rather than being decoded into one.
          //
          // The NAME is decoded to a fixed point (codex PR #1727 round 7):
          // "%256bey" decodes once to "%6bey", not "key". A name that still
          // carries an escape after the loop fails closed, and one that will
          // not decode throws into the catch below, which also fails closed.
          if (onPlayground && !/^[1-9][0-9]*$/.test(rawValue)) {
            // FORM decoding on every pass, not only the first: %2Bkey%2B
            // decodes to +key+, which is " key " (codex PR #1727 round 9).
            var pgKey = decodedKey;
            for (var pd = 0; pd < 8 && /%[0-9A-Fa-f]{2}|\+/.test(pgKey); pd++) {
              pgKey = decodeURIComponent(pgKey.replace(/\+/g, ' '));
            }
            // Trimmed and folded as common.QueryKeyMatches does (TrimSpace
            // includes U+0085; EqualFold folds U+212A to k, as toLowerCase
            // does), and a name still carrying an escape or a + after the
            // bound fails closed (codex PR #1727 rounds 8 and 10).
            // Any % at all: "%25key" decodes to "%key", which Go's next
            // decode rejects and fails closed on (codex PR #1727 round 11).
            var pgUnfinished = /[%+]/.test(pgKey);
            pgKey = pgKey.replace(/^[\s\u0085]+|[\s\u0085]+$/g, '');
            if (pgUnfinished || pgKey.toLowerCase() === 'key') {
              sensitiveQuery = true;
              break;
            }
          }
        }
      } catch (e) {
        sensitiveQuery = true;
      }
      // Locale-stripped path for the exact/prefix auth checks below. A
      // localized URL like /zh-CN/auth?code_challenge=… or
      // /ja/accept-invite?token=… is served as the SPA shell (IsKnownSPARoute
      // strips the locale) and LocaleFallback preserves the query while it
      // client-redirects to the bare path — so this boot guard, which runs
      // FIRST, must normalize the locale prefix or the token/PII-bearing URL
      // reaches the tags before the redirect (codex round 15). The
      // redeem/boost/squad regexes below already embed the optional prefix.
      var pNoLocale = p.replace(/^\/[A-Za-z]{2}(-[A-Za-z0-9]+)?(?=\/)/, '').toLowerCase();
      // The public /redeem/:code claim route carries a redeemable bearer
      // voucher code in the path. Skip third-party analytics so GTM/Meta Pixel
      // never capture the code via page_location/referrer. Matched with an
      // optional leading locale segment (/zh-CN/redeem/:code etc., served by
      // the /:loc/* SPA fallback) and requires /redeem to be a full path
      // segment so /redeemed... is not caught.
      var isRedeem = /^(\/[A-Za-z]{2}(-[A-Za-z0-9]+)?)?\/redeem(\/|$)/i.test(p);
      // The /b/:token boost share landing carries the sharer's tap-scoped
      // token in the path. Same page_location leak class as /redeem, so the
      // cold click must not reach GTM/Meta before the stub redirects. The
      // sessionStorage 'boost_token' breadcrumb deliberately does NOT join
      // the pendingRedeem-style blanket suppression: the token grants TAP
      // rights only (never read/claim — a different bearer class than a
      // redeemable voucher code), and suppressing all analytics through the
      // /register leg would blind the signup conversion pixel for exactly
      // the boost-referred cohort the growth loop measures.
      var isBoostShare = /^(\/[A-Za-z]{2}(-[A-Za-z0-9]+)?)?\/b\//i.test(p);
      // The /s/:token squad-share landing carries a join-rights bearer token in
      // the path — same page_location leak class as /b, so the cold click must
      // not reach GTM/Meta before the redirect stub replaces the URL (codex).
      var isSquadShare = /^(\/[A-Za-z]{2}(-[A-Za-z0-9]+)?)?\/s\//i.test(p);
      // /compliance/share/<token> is a PUBLIC, no-login report view whose path
      // token is an unauthenticated bearer capability — it authorizes reading
      // the report and (when enabled) downloading the artifact. Same
      // page_location leak class as /b and /s, so no tag may see it (codex).
      var isComplianceShare = /^(\/[A-Za-z]{2}(-[A-Za-z0-9]+)?)?\/compliance\/share(\/|$)/i.test(p);
      // /share/<token> is the routing-report landing the card's QR resolves to.
      // The token is an unauthenticated bearer capability over the frozen
      // snapshot, and the reader is ALWAYS signed out (it arrives from a
      // screenshot, a social unfurl or a scan), so the cold load is exactly the
      // moment a tag would capture page_location. Same class as /compliance/share.
      var isRoutingShare = /^(\/[A-Za-z]{2}(-[A-Za-z0-9]+)?)?\/share(\/|$)/i.test(p);
      // /rig/<token> is the rig-share landing — the recipient's first view of
      // somebody else's machine. Same bearer class as /share and MORE than it
      // grants: the routing share exposes a frozen report, this token authorizes
      // running inference on the owner's own GPU until the link expires or its
      // request cap runs out. The reader is ALWAYS signed out and always arrives
      // cold (the link was sent to them), so the parse-time load is exactly the
      // moment a tag would capture page_location — and BearerRouteHead cannot
      // help, because it is a React component that mounts long after the tags in
      // this head have run.
      //
      // /rig-bench/<token> is deliberately NOT suppressed. It is the one page on
      // this surface built to be posted, indexed and unfurled — a frozen
      // measurement with no account data behind it and no access granted — so it
      // carries no BearerRouteHead either (web/src/App.jsx). Suppressing it would
      // blind exactly the growth loop it exists to feed. The trailing
